newsitem.title: FINLAND: MERITA SURPISED BY MORTGAGE DEMAND - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: MERITA SURPISED BY MORTGAGE DEMAND - PAPER.

text.p: Demand for mortgages has been higher than expected, the chief economist of Finland's largest banking group Merita Oy was quoted as saying in business daily Kauppalehti on Thursday.

"Nobody had been able to expect this strong a pace. The six-month run of growth in new mortgages tells about a turn which is not expected to be reversed," the paper quoted Merita chief ecnomist Juha Ahtola as saying.
Banks are also encouraged by high consumer confidence, the paper said.

"The best thing about the trend is that demand is real. True house buyers are on the move and this is not about rearranging old credits which would only superficially improve statistics," Ahtola said.

According to the Bank of Finland's latest Finance Markets review dated November 12, new mortgages totalled 2.40 billion markka in September -- the highest since August 1990 -- and the stock of outstanding mortgages rose 500 million markka to 96.5 billion.
The stock turned to a rise in June, having bottomed out at 94.1 billion in May, and a 1.3 billion markka jump was registered in August, the central bank said.

In 1989, when the Finnish economy was still booming before hitting a wall in 1990/1991 to fall into its deepest abyss since World War II, the amount of mortgages granted per month was over three billion markka.
